newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan withdraws monopoly on wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan withdraws monopoly on wheat imports.

text.p: Pakistan has withdrawn a concession that gave the national shipping company the right to match the lowest bid on wheat freight tenders, a company executive said on Wednesday.
He said the Pakistan National Shipping Corporation (PNSC) would have to join open international bidding for wheat shipment contracts for a three-month trial period.
"Now we will bid in the open market for the wheat imports for Pakistan as any other company from April to May," said the PNSC executive, who asked not to be named.
The government gave the first right of refusal to the state-run PNSC in 1994.
Pakistan was expected to decide later on Wednesday on a tender for about 330,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian soft white wheat for shipment between May 20 and June 10.
Officials say Pakistan is likely to import about four million tonnes of wheat in the next 12 months.

The executive said rates quoted by the PNSC for wheat imports had been "realistic and competitive", but the Ministry of Agriculture and Food had insisted on open bidding because of a slump in the international shipping industry.
However, some wheat trade sources said the previous system had resulted in a lack of serious bidding for wheat freight deals and had led to Pakistan paying inflated freight rates.
"We have the expertise, the manpower and facilities to handle wheat imports, but if the food ministry wants to try other options, the PNSC will compete in the open market," the executive said.
"The food ministry has little experience in such deals and they could be taken for a ride by foreign shipping companies for wheat imports," he added.
The executive said the PNSC had brought 104 wheat shipments to Pakistan since 1994, of which 90 were on time. The rest suffered delays of one to 10 days.
He said Pakistan's only private shipping company, Tristar Shipping Lines Ltd, favoured the PNSC's first right of refusal because it is frequently given business by PNSC.
He could not say how much PNSC might lose in revenue following the withdrawal of the concession.
